LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD's top-level scope only contains variable assignments (pkgname, pkgver, source, sha256sums, etc.) and function definitions (prepare, build, package). There is no `pkgver()` function, no command substitutions, no code that executes during sourcing of the file. The `source` array uses HTTPS URLs with valid SHA-256 checksums, so `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` will fetch and verify the downloads without executing any malicious code. The `makepkg --printsrcinfo` command simply prints the SRCINFO, which is also safe. The functions `prepare()`, `build()`, and `package()` are not executed due to the `--noprepare` and `--nobuild` flags.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>No malicious code in top-level scope; safe to fetch sources.</summary>

audits.body:
Cloning https://aur.archlinux.org/jagex-launcher.git...
Cloned jagex-launcher
Analyzing jagex-launcher AUR package with qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-2507
Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines standard sources: an AppImage binary from a known Jagex domain and a license file. The `source` array uses a direct HTTPS URL to fetch the AppImage, which is expected for AppImage-based packages. The checksums are provided and not set to 'SKIP', so the integrity of the downloaded files will be verified during the sourcing process. There are no command substitutions, `pkgver()` function overrides, or top-level executable statements outside of variable assignments. The `prepare()`, `build()`, and `package()` functions contain only post-extraction and installation logic that will not execute due to the `--noprepare` and `--nobuild` flags. Therefore, sourcing this PKGBUILD and downloading the sources poses no risk of executing untrusted code during this phase.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
No dangerous code executes during source fetch and parse
</summary>
</security_assessment>

LLM auditresponse for JAGEX-EULA:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The provided file is the End User Licence Agreement (EULA) for the Jagex Launcher and associated software, including RuneScape and related games. It is a legal document outlining the terms under which users may use Jagex's software, and it contains no executable code, scripts, or system-level instructions.

This file does not represent a software package or build script but rather a policy document detailing user rights, restrictions on reverse engineering, intellectual property ownership, disclaimers of warranty, and rules regarding modifications and server hosting. It includes standard EULA clauses such as limitations of liability, export controls, and termination rights.

There are no commands, network calls, file operations, or obfuscated content present. The document references third-party integrations (e.g., Epic Games Account requirement for RuneScape: Dragonwilds), but these are functional requirements of the upstream application, not evidence of malicious behavior in the AUR package context. References to mods and user-generated content are part of Jagex’s official modding policy and do not indicate supply-chain risks.

As this is a static licensing text with no executable or system-interacting components, there is no security risk posed by this file in the context of an AUR package audit.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
Non-executable license document; no malicious content
</summary>
</security_assessment>

[1/3] Reviewing .SRCINFO, PKGBUILD...
+ Reviewed JAGEX-EULA. Status: SAFE -- Non-executable license document; no malicious content
LLM auditresponse for .SRCINFO:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The `.SRCINFO` file is a metadata file used by Arch Linux's AUR to describe the package build configuration. It lists sources, checksums, dependencies, and other package attributes. In this case, the file references an AppImage binary from `rs-launcher-updates.runescape.com`, which is consistent with the official Jagex launcher distribution domain as seen in the `url` field (`https://osrs.runescape.com/download`). The source URL points to a specific versioned release (0.1.6), enabling reproducible builds.

Checksums for both the AppImage and the EULA file are provided using SHA-256, a secure hashing algorithm. There are no signs of obfuscated URLs, suspicious scripts, or network operations that could indicate malicious behavior. The use of `!strip` is common for binaries like AppImages where symbol stripping is unnecessary or harmful. No executable code or commands are present in this file — it is purely declarative metadata.

All elements align with standard AUR packaging practices. The sources are from expected domains related to the software, and there is no evidence of injected payloads, backdoors, or unauthorized data exfiltration mechanisms. While the AppImage itself is a prebuilt binary (which limits transparency), the `.SRCINFO` does not introduce additional risks beyond the inherent trust in the upstream source.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
No malicious content; standard AUR metadata
</summary>
</security_assessment>

[2/3] Reviewing PKGBUILD...
+ Reviewed .SRCINFO. Status: SAFE -- No malicious content; standard AUR metadata
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD fetches a prebuilt AppImage from Jagex's official domain (`rs-launcher-updates.runescape.com`) and extracts it to install the launcher system-wide. It correctly sets permissions, adjusts the `.desktop` file to disable desktop integration at runtime, and installs icons, licenses, and symlinks in standard locations. All operations are transparent and follow standard packaging practices for AppImages on Arch Linux.

Checksums are provided and match the expected hash of the AppImage and the EULA file, ensuring integrity. The source URL is from the official Jagex domain, and no obfuscated or suspicious commands (e.g., `curl|bash`, `eval`, or base64-encoded payloads) are present. The use of `chmod +x` and `--appimage-extract` is necessary for AppImage handling and is not inherently risky in this context.

While the package installs a binary blob (the AppImage), this is expected for official launcher distributions. There is no evidence of data exfiltration, unauthorized network requests, or injected code. The license file is included separately and matches Jagex's EULA. No post-install hooks or system modifications beyond standard desktop integration are performed.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
Standard AppImage packaging with official source and valid checksums</summary>
</security_assessment>
